Hi Sophia — thanks for the worksheet and the clear numbers. Quick summary from our side and a proposed approach before we schedule a call: 

1) Reservation + burst model (recommended)
   - Reserved slab: size for ~1.25x steady-state -> 100 workers (covers most sustained traffic and gives some headroom).
   - Burst pool: pooled ephemeral capacity sized to cover typical peak multiples; recommend initial burst pool equal to 1.5x steady-state (~120 workers) behind a prewarm window so we can spin in <60s for hot paths.

2) Autoscale & priority rules (ops-friendly defaults)
   - Reservation enforcement: reserved slab has guaranteed slots; burst can be throttled when global utilization > 85%.
   - Preemption policy: ephemeral burst instances evict by lowest priority tag; reserved customer tasks are pinned and not preemptible.
   - Target utilization for autoscaler: 60–70% on reserved slab to avoid latency cliffs; burst activation at sustained queue depth > 5s for 30s window.

3) QoS and SLOs
   - Keep a short KV cache warm for top templates to reduce token compute during peaks.
   - If 95th latency approaches SLA, fallback to a smaller gen model variant for non-critical routes.

I put these in a one-page proposal and a short ops checklist (attached). If this looks reasonable, I can loop in Marissa for pricing/contracting and Ben for ops runbook.

Proposed meeting: Fri 18 Jun, 3pm PT. Does that work?

Hi Sophia / team — great to meet earlier on the call. Summary of the proposed commercial + ops alignment we agreed to: 

1) Commit structure (Q4 initial term, 12 months)
   - Reserved slab: 100-worker equivalent (monthly committed spend line item).
   - Burst pool: guaranteed bucket of 80 workers with two-tier pricing (first block discounted).

2) Autoscale & SLO addendum (to be added to SOW)

   - Prewarm SLA: Redwood targets a <60s warm-up for hot lanes; we will instrument with tracing and telemetry hooks.
   - Credits: if prewarm >120s during a production peak, Aperture receives a service credit applied to the following invoice (credit % TBD in SOW).

3) Ops runbook deliverables (owned by Redwood)
   - Pre-deploy checklist, traffic ramp steps, and throttling knobs.
   - A one-week burn-in window where burst gating is relaxed for onboarding.

Next steps: Aditya to send a redline-friendly SOW and a short runbook draft. Procurement — if you can share Aperture's PO template, we can map billing terms.
